observations.content: pi-web-access tool code located at ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-web-access/ with files extract.ts, index.ts, youtube-extract.ts, video-extract.ts, utils.ts
video-extract.ts extractVideoFrame runs execFileSync ffmpeg -ss <seconds> -i <filePath> -frames:v 1 -f image2pipe -vcodec mjpeg pipe:1 with maxBuffer 5MB and timeout 10000ms; returns base64 JPEG
youtube-extract.ts getYouTubeStreamInfo runs yt-dlp --print duration -g URL (no -f flag) with 15000ms timeout, takes lines[0]=duration and lines[1]=video stream URL
youtube-extract.ts extractFrameFromStream feeds the stream URL directly to ffmpeg (-ss seconds -i streamUrl -frames:v 1 -f image2pipe -vcodec mjpeg pipe:1) with 30000ms timeout, NOT a downloaded file
Manual identical ffmpeg command on downloaded me.mp4.webm (320x240) succeeded: exit 0, valid 13786-byte JPEG at /tmp/pipeout.jpg

Root cause chain found: yt-dlp requires a JS runtime to solve YouTube signatures; without runtime, format list is empty, --get-url returns empty, ffmpeg opens a nonexistent input and errors with the misleading 'ffmpeg failed' banner instead of the real yt-dlp error
Confirmed: yt-dlp without JS runtime gave 'No supported JavaScript runtime could be found... requested format is not available', while with --js-runtimes node the video URL was returned
Fix applied: created /home/coder/.config/yt-dlp/config containing '--js-runtimes node' (node is at /usr/local/bin/node); this fixes the tool globally without editing the npm package
config file confirmed loaded via yt-dlp -v: 'User config /home/coder/.config/yt-dlp/config: [--js-runtimes node]' and 'JS runtimes: node-24.16.0'
yt-dlp -f 'b' --get-url proved flaky: 1 of 3 calls succeeded because YouTube intermittently hides the muxed format (PO token / A-B testing)
Tool's exact call yt-dlp --print duration -g URL (no -f, default bv*+ba/b format) was stable 3/3 after the config fix, printing duration 19 plus two DASH stream URLs
Real failure isolated: static johnvansickle ffmpeg 7.0.2 segfaulted (exit 139, SIGSEGV) when reading the DASH stream URL directly, producing an empty output file

Replaced ffmpeg/ffprobe in ~/.local/bin with BtbN FFmpeg-Builds master build (ffmpeg version N-126335-gb32f8d1c23-20260830), downloaded from github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds releases as ffmpeg-master-latest-linux64-gpl.tar.xz
New BtbN ffmpeg handled the DASH stream: exit 0, valid 320x240 JPEG (comment Lavc63.8.101) at /tmp/pipeout4.jpg
Fetch_content tool then succeeded end-to-end on the YouTube video: 3 frames extracted from 0:08-0:18; resolved the 'ffmpeg failed: banner' error
